To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) deconvolution layers are an effective way to add additional context in object detection, and 2) that a new output module is required to fully leverage this additional context.

(1) Deconvolution layers can be added in a principled fashion to improve detection performance, especially for small and occluded objects; (2) Deconvolutional layers can be used in a single shot detector to introduce additional context into the detection pipeline, improving performance over a state of the arts SSD and ResNet; (3) Deconvolution can be used to improve detection performance in a principled manner, and is an interesting direction for further research.

1) a naive combination of a state of the-art classifier with a fast detection system does not perform as expected and 2) adding deconvolutional layers and a new output layer to SSD+ResNet101 enables the combination to outperform the current state of the art.

the following questions: (a) How can we introduce additional context into a state of the ar t detection system? (b) How do we implement such an approach in a principled way?

the following questions: (1) How can we improve detection accuracy by adding additional context? (2) What are the key components that are required to achieve this? and (3) What are the implications of these results on future detection research?
how to combine a state of art classifier with an object detector and then how to introduce context into this system.
